title: Universal Transmitter: Operation and Shared Circuits
introduction: The universal transmitter stores a hand-held transmitter's code so a visor button can send the corresponding radio signal. I think of the buttons as labeled memory slots: pressing a button calls up what was learned for that slot. This overview explains storage, transmission and the shared visor circuits. Programming steps and indicator-lamp meanings are outside its scope.

edits.text: Operation begins with learning and storing a hand-held transmitter code.
edits.why: Stored information connects the learning function to later button-operated transmission.

edits.text: The universal transmitter learns a hand-held transmitter's radio-frequency code and stores it in memory. It has 3 buttons and an indicator lamp. After a code has been stored, pressing its corresponding button makes the universal transmitter emit the hand-held transmitter's radio frequency. It can store 3 unique transmitter codes at a time. The universal transmitter and the LH (left-hand) vanity mirror lamp are both part of the LH sun visor and share the same power and ground circuits.
edits.why: The button-to-stored-code relationship explains how the transmitter selects what to send. I also keep the shared electrical paths in mind: power supplies both devices, and ground provides their electrical return path. Their common circuits are useful context for later diagnosis, but do not identify a failed component on their own.
